equation_summary: Two coupled matrix states S and M, each [K,V] (naive.py:46-65): w_t = -(v_t - p_t^T S_{t-1}) (prediction read off the memory state with separate key p); M_t = mu_t * M_{t-1} + (eta_t * k_t) ⊗ w_t (momentum state, scalar decay mu); S_t = alpha_t * S_{t-1} - beta_t * M_t (memory updated by the freshly-written momentum — the coupling); o_t = (scale*q_t)^T S_t, read after both updates. alpha, mu, beta are per-head scalars (exp of log params); eta scales k. Initial S and M are separate operands and the final state is the stacked pair (naive.py:37-43,69).
state_shape: two coupled [B,H,K,V] matrices (S memory + M momentum)
ledger_verdicts: CONFIRM call graph E[Q/K/p/alpha and optional norms] ; B[K2 coupled memory+momentum states] ; E[output]: the mixer genuinely carries two states with S_t depending on the just-updated M_t (naive.py:59-60) — a coupled-state descriptor, not a single K2 state.
CONFIRM 'no one-matrix alias': S and M have independent decay (alpha vs mu) and independent initial/final state (naive.py:23-24,37-43,69 stacks [S,M]); eliminating M changes the law.

CONFIRM blockers: both states and default source modes preserved; note the chunk reference (naive.py:126-197) needs log-cumsum-exp gamma masks combining alpha/mu/beta — the coupled-state VJP envelope is nontrivial and correctly blocked.
axis: A8 coupled multi-state transition (memory state S fed by momentum state M within one token step)
direction_justification: The defining property is a closed typed coupling of two matrix states with per-state scalar decays — reusable (e.g. Titans-style memory+momentum, row 039) but outside the single-state U2 contract, so it is an axis.
open_questions: Whether the descriptor should treat M as a first-class state bundle member with its own initial/final state and cotangent (source does: final_state = stack([S,M])) — and how cross-state VJP flows are represented.
Whether eta (k-scaling on the momentum write) is a per-head scalar everywhere or has channel variants in other modes.
